drivingQuestion: With which formula should one take leave of the dead?
outcomeNote: A dictum with its prooftext; the paired rule for the living stands in the preceding unit, outside this one.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין הַלֵּוִי: הַנִּפְטָר מִן הַמֵּת אַל יֹאמַר לוֹ ״לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם״, אֶלָּא ״לֵךְ בְּשָׁלוֹם״, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה תָּבוֹא אֶל אֲבֹתֶיךָ בְּשָׁלוֹם״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Avin HaLevi also said: One who takes leave from a dead person should not say to him: Go to peace, but rather,» one should say: «Go in peace, as it is stated: “But you shall go to your fathers in peace”» (Genesis 15:15).

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי אבין הלוי: הנפטר מן המת
moves.summary: a further dictum of R' Avin HaLevi, inverting for the dead the formula just given for the living
moves.about: the prooftext for the formula used in taking leave of the dead

moves.summary: Abraham is told he will go to his fathers בשלום
moves.about: that one takes leave of the dead with לך בשלום and not לך לשלום, the reverse of the rule for the living

edges.cueHe: הנפטר מן המת אל יאמר לו ״לך לשלום״, אלא ״לך בשלום״
edges.about: that one takes leave of the dead with לך בשלום and not לך לשלום, the reverse of the rule for the living
